feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support a Digital Communications/Strategy Lead profile.  
- Good credibility and substance: Drupal migration, analytics stack, studio buildout, AI-enabled search, and large-scale publishing environment all signal real operational leadership.  
- Writing is generally polished and easy to follow, with strong action verbs and mission-driven framing.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (growth %, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, campaign results, budget/team size).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix consistency/style issues: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; keep serial commas consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); standardize punctuation in bullets. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specific positioning, cleaner phrasing, and less overlap with the competencies and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for grammar and tighter style.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and sector fit: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Trim channel lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) since these are covered in experience and skills; emphasize outcomes and scope instead.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience advancing web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, leadership-level phrases and reduce tool/functional overlap: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Content operations & editorial governance • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web operations & CMS management • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow design & systems improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, video & live event production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and clearer wording.
- Replace “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Workflow design & systems improvement” unless you want to signal a more technical/enterprise architect profile.
- Keep terminology consistent with the rest of the CV: use either “cross-department” or “cross-functional,” not both.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Web & CMS administration,” analytics, and multimedia are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
- “Stakeholder coordination” and advocacy messaging are also repeated in the header and Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around scope, seniority, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-led bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics + governance/usability into one operations-improvement bullet.
- Rephrase for outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign experiences and reusable microsite/toolkit components that improved publishing speed, consistency, and member access to resources.” Add metrics if available.
- Make the AI/search work a standout final bullet: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX.” Add launch status, content volume, or user impact if possible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search,” “microsite structures,” and campaign examples duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new/current in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the website modernization as the lead bullet and make outcome language stronger: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-based; add metrics if available: email growth/open rates, social engagement, video output, event reach, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built analytics and publishing systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep the CV item focused on organizational impact, not production detail.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper verbs and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead line to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Replace vague process language with concrete impact if possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning workflows spanning communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards bullet.
- “Weekly video updates” echoes the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent role bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership themes and avoid repeating platform/operations language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Reframe for executive scope and outcomes, not task areas:  
- Enterprise digital strategy  
- Content governance and editorial operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector and advocacy communications  
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider replacing “messaging” with “communications” for a more senior, systems-level tone.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is good, but “content governance and editorial operations” reads broader and aligns better with recent leadership roles.
- If space allows, add one sharper differentiator such as “organizational change leadership” or “digital transformation leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with multiple work-experience bullets on storytelling/editorial coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and execution themes rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Consider dropping WordPress here unless it is important for target roles; it appears less central than recent Drupal-led work.
- If space allows, sharpen one item to outcome-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid listing the same platforms in both sections with equal detail.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger senior-level wording: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, performance analysis and experimentation”

- Avoid repeating every tool here if the Technical + IT section already lists them in full.

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” It should be tightened to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than generic tool/task terms.

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent experience is strongest in Drupal-led modernization, this item should emphasize depth/order and trim lower-value entries.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling strength: “Drupal (enterprise migration, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If formatting allows, add brief qualifiers only for strongest platforms, especially Drupal, to connect to the 10,000+ page migration and enterprise publishing context.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was not materially used in recent roles; it feels lighter-weight than the rest and may dilute seniority.
- Keep this item concise and platform-only; save implementation detail for the adjacent technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same CMS tools.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating descriptors here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery
- Add a second grouping: Technical delivery & integrations: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language elsewhere or in a parenthetical here, e.g., “for Drupal-based sites, analytics deployment, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioned naming consistently; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; avoid repeating automation language across both sections

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize actual automation platforms over general collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to foreground systems work: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” if you keep Slack/Teams/project tools here.
- Group similar tools to reduce listiness: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- If space is tight, cut the least differentiating tools first: Basecamp, Trello, Slack, Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them in multiple prominent sections unless this list is shortened.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are lower-value than your stronger technical platforms and may dilute impact.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo work. It should signal enterprise email operations, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience engagement and campaign delivery**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **used to support newsletters and advocacy communications reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep platform names only if he has hands-on/admin experience; otherwise move less-used tools to a secondary “Familiar with” line or remove

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo bullets about newsletters; avoid repeating outcomes here unless adding a short scale qualifier
- If Dynamics 365 was not central in recent roles, consider dropping it to keep the section aligned with strongest, most recent experience

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building, production, and early platform work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, frequency of video updates, or team support metrics.
- Tighten the second sentence around direct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s daily work.”
- If possible, add one outcome: improved publishing speed, expanded in-house production capacity, increased audience reach, or reduced reliance on vendors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or establishing the format here, then scaling it later.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; specify early process-building to distinguish it from later governance leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation/program support plus that first-of-its-kind multimedia initiative.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add clearer ownership and tighter phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim vague wording like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific output if possible, e.g. web features, reports, interviews, or promotional assets.
- If available, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, projects coordinated, or audience/reach.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; save management/operations emphasis for 2015–2024 roles.
